mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.63%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) signals a decrease in consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when RSAFS drops > 2% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2% YoY and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, the real interest rate becomes negative, which stimulates investment and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when CPIAUCSL > 2% YoY and FEDFUNDS < 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 100k MoM and UNRATE increases > 0.3pp
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when PAYEMS decreases > 100k MoM and UNRATE increases > 0.3pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases > 5% YoY, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) combined with a rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a supply-side recovery, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases > 0.5% QoQ and INDPRO increases > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when GDPC1 decreases > 0.5% QoQ and INDPRO increases > 0.5% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.
